title: Group Anagrams
hints: two words are anagrams if and only if they become identical once you sort their letters - what does that suggest as a grouping key?
for each word, compute a canonical signature (its letters sorted alphabetically), and use that signature as a hash map key mapping to the list of original words sharing it
after one pass building the map, each value in the map is already a complete anagram group - no further comparison needed
for the final deterministic output, sort the words within each group alphabetically, then sort the groups themselves by their first word before joining into the encoded string
commonMistakes: using a letter frequency count as the key without normalizing it into a comparable/hashable form, or accidentally treating two different frequency counts as equal
forgetting to sort the words within each group before joining, producing output that depends on input order and isn't deterministic
forgetting to sort the groups themselves before joining, so equivalent inputs in a different order produce different-looking output
splitting the input string incorrectly (e.g. not handling a single trailing word correctly), producing an extra empty word
using string concatenation of unsorted characters as the key, which fails to recognize e.g. 'eat' and 'ate' as anagrams

content.problemStatement:
You're given a list of lowercase words, given as a single space-delimited
string `strs`. Every word belongs to exactly one group, where a group
contains every word that is an anagram of every other word in it, using
exactly the same letters and counts in any order.

**Group the words, then encode the result as a single string: within each group, sort the words alphabetically and join them with commas, sort the groups themselves alphabetically by their own first word, and join the groups with a pipe character `"|"`.**

This makes the output fully deterministic regardless of the input order.
constraints: every word consists of lowercase English letters only
notes: every word is a unique anagram of every other (all end up in one group)
no two words share any anagram relationship (every word is its own group)
duplicate identical words (they anagram with themselves and belong together)

sampleTestCases.explanation: eat/tea/ate share letters a,e,t; tan/nat share a,n,t; bat is alone
no two words share the same letters, so every word is its own group
a single word is trivially its own group

optimal.time: O(n * k log k) where n is the number of words and k is the max word length, dominated by sorting each word's letters
optimal.space: O(n * k) for the hash map storing all words
optimal.pattern: hash map keyed by each word's sorted-letters signature, so every anagram of a word maps to the same key

bruteForce.approach: for every pair of words, check whether they're anagrams by sorting both and comparing, then union words into groups based on these pairwise matches
bruteForce.time: O(n^2 * k log k) where n is the number of words and k is the max word length, from the pairwise comparisons
bruteForce.space: O(n * k) to store the groups
